examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability on an Unbounded Interval Using the Complement
examples.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z\sim N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z \geq -1.16).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/cac32ab36217820b63574e011488721bf57652fa63b4cbb7e5029fb54ce26243.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z),$ 

$$
P(Z \leq z) = \Phi(z).
$$

Since the total area under the graph equals $1,$ we can express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -1.16) & =1-P(Z<-1.16) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.16)\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/48adcb6bd3b0d12b9bc935b2414d615e0014d905b89a9f7d632306cd30f08580.png)

From the table, we know that

$$
\Phi(-1.16) =  0.1230.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -1.16) & =1-Φ(-1.16) \\  & =1-0.1230 \\  & =0.8770.\end{aligned}
$$

If $Z∼N(0,1),$ then by the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Also, since $Z$ is continuous, 

$$
P(Z<1.48)=P(Z\le 1.48)=Φ(1.48).
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/83df9b5a21d25104979949ceb25bffa7fca1ded99b671ca3c530b9cb94d4194a.png)

Now, we determine the value of $Φ(1.48)$ from the table:

- We first select the row that corresponds to $1.4$ and the column that corresponds to $0.08.$

- Then, we take the value that lies at the intersection:

| $z$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8980\,$ | $\,0.8997\,$ | $\,0.9015\,$ |
| $\,1.3\,$ | $\,0.9147\,$ | $\,0.9162\,$ | $\,0.9177\,$ |
| $\,1.4\,$ | $\,0.9292\,$ | $\,0.9306\,$ | $\,0.9319\,$ |

Therefore, according to the table, we have

$$
P(Z\le 1.48)=Φ(1.48)=0.9306.
$$
